rules: No orange is legible on brand green — display 2.48:1, default 1.87:1, rust 1.29:1. On green use text/inverse (6.6:1) or bg/page (7.8:1). Orange on green is for non-text graphics only.
Orange on green is for graphics only — dividers, rules, fills. Never text. Footer dividers use accent/display at 2px.
Orange leader line marks a section header and the active nav item. On green it is never the sole state signal — active also carries brighter text and a heavier rule.
Section headings are 36px Bitter Bold across every page and the footer tagline. Colour varies, size does not.
Hover on a nav destination is the orange 2px rule; active is the same orange at 4px. Button hover is a 2px lift plus a fill darken — never a shadow.
Sponsor options are full-width Tier Rows grouped into four buckets (Premium, Meal, Hole, Golf Entry). Rows not cards — tiers carry 2 to 6 benefits and cards made that ragged.
Registration page nav: Register button becomes a plain Home link, and no destination is marked active because Registration is not listed.
Availability badges show spots remaining, not caps. Limited tone at 2 or fewer, SoldOut at 0. The number is the urgency.
Groups table: hole is the row, Group A and Group B are the columns. No tee times — shotgun start means everyone tees off at once.
Groups table: hole sits in a 48px green scorecard chip, group number is 19px Bitter Bold, rows zebra on bg/panel, a hairline divides Group A from Group B. Highlighted row flips the chip to orange.
Group cards own their own fill and border so a name match can highlight one group without lighting the whole hole row.
Contact is a plain list, not a card. Contact details are read once and acted on — a button adds a step where a mailto link on plain text does not.
Form Field gained a Type=Upload with a dashed dropzone — 24 variants total. Logo upload requires high-res, vector preferred, because the file lands on physical signage.

Two register forms. Sponsor: Company Information / Player Information / Comments. Golfer: Your Information (incl. payment) / Team Information / Comments — no company section. Payment options are Check, Cash, Venmo only.
Name fields are single inputs with a 'First and last' helper — never split first/last. Form headers carry only a Back to sponsor packages button.
Sponsor Player Information and golfer Your Information are two-column. Golfer Team Information stays full-width single fields.
Form inputs use bg/field (white), not bg/page. On a cream card bg/page is ~1.1:1 against the card and the box is defined by its border alone.

Kyle widened every Home container to 1312; Groups (lookup and pairings table, were 1180) and the six register-form cards (were 1080) were normalised up to match on 2026-08-20. The track is deliberately wider than the ribbon and clipped, with white edge fades both sides, so it reads as mid-scroll. White ground is a requirement, not a style choice — several sponsor logos are low-resolution and need white behind them.

On green-ground social posts, place the logo bare — the green corner block is invisible on green and masks the keyline where it crosses. The corner block is for light and cream grounds only.
Social CTAs say 'link in bio', never a URL. The site has no public domain yet; fore-grant.netlify.app is scaffolding, not a published address.
Orange text fails on green in social too — post 1's eyebrow and post 6's count both had to move off orange. On green the count sits white-on-orange inside a chip (accent/default + white, 4.66:1).

Meet Grant story sits in a 2px orange keyline box (radius lg, 40px padding) with the 'His Fight Is Our Fight' glove logo at its right — the flyer's treatment. The glove ties the section to Grant himself and keeps it clear of the tournament wordmark, which is the whole reason it is there rather than the Fore Grant badge.

Third-party logos are the ONE exception to the closed palette: the San Vicente Resort mark is blue and green and must never be recoloured to fit, and sponsor logos keep their own colours. They sit on white — that is what the ticker's white ribbon and the shout-out post's white panel are for. An exception for a mark someone else owns is not a licence to add a hue anywhere else.

Rasterising Adobe files drifts colour: 'G$ Fight.ai' came out #de5937 / #050707 instead of #F05323 / #000000. Normalise every imported asset against the swatch card before it goes into Figma — assets/logos/his-fight-is-our-fight.png is already normalised.

Find Us ends with the San Vicente Resort logo under the map — the 'Get directions' Nav Link was removed 2026-08-20. The venue logo is the link target: it goes to the course site, so directions are one hop away and the venue requirement is met without a second row of text.

Subpage nav uses 'Logo — Horizontal Negative' at 165x64 inside the 100px bar, not the stacked badge. The badge crammed to 104x76 was unreadable. The bar's counterAxisSizingMode is FIXED at 100 — it hugs its logo otherwise and the 100px rule silently breaks.

Icons are Phosphor, 44px, one per card at the top: trophy = Contests, ticket = Ways to Win, hamburger = Meals. Imported via createNodeFromSvg so they stay editable vectors, and their fills bind to a token rather than carrying the source #000000.

Icons on the dark green CTA are bg/page light (7.8:1), not orange. Orange icons on green measured the same 2.48:1 the text rule already warns about and read muddy — the rule covers decorative marks too once they carry meaning.
Card icons are 96px, not 44 — at 44 they read as UI chrome; at 96 they read as design elements, which is the job here.

The dark green CTA carries three decorative golf balls, not meaning-bearing icons. Because they are purely decorative, orange IS permitted on green under the graphics exemption — but light is the recommendation: the Register button should be the only orange in that card, or the CTA signal gets diluted.

Day-of cards and the Day-of section must HUG vertically, never a fixed height. They were pinned at 438 and were silently clipping Kyle's raffle and 50/50 ticket prices before the icons were ever added. Three cards stay even by pinning all to the tallest measured height.

A group lookup match is dark green with light text, never the old orange tint — a warm tint on a light ground read as an error state. Orange survives only as the card's edge. Both Pairing Group Highlighted variants and the bespoke card in the Groups table were changed together; they are separate nodes and drift apart if only one is touched.

Dark green + light text is THE hover language across the site — buttons darken, tier rows go dark, group matches go dark. Anything that highlights should join that language rather than inventing a colour.

Nav Link has FOUR states per tone: Default, Hover, Active, ActiveMuted. The current page is underlined at rest; the moment a DIFFERENT item is hovered its underline drops out, so only one underline is on screen and it always belongs to what the pointer is addressing. Colour is NOT dropped — the current page keeps its brighter text so the user never loses their place. The 4px rule is reserved in every state so nothing reflows.

Binding a colour variable to a STROKE does not always resolve even when the variable's scopes include STROKE_COLOR — the highlighted group card rendered black with a valid accent/default binding. Set the paint's LITERAL colour to the token's resolved value AND bind it. Check strokes visually; a correct-looking boundVariables entry is not proof.

Social posts go flat when every frame shares one skeleton. The levers that fix it, in order of payoff: (1) photography with a directional scrim, (2) extreme scale on the one number that matters, (3) a hard two-tone split instead of even margins, (4) argyle as a full-bleed band rather than a 24px trim, (5) one hot orange block per frame instead of orange sprinkled thin.

Photo scrims are DIRECTIONAL, never flat. A flat green scrim at 0.78 killed the photo entirely and at 0.55 greyed it out. A left-heavy gradient (0.96 -> 0.86 -> 0.30 brand green, left to right) keeps type on solid green and the photograph alive where there is no type. Logos and small type must sit in the dark end.
Social alternates are built as NEW frames on a second row (y=1400) beside the originals, never by overwriting them — the set is for comparison until Kyle picks a direction.
Social row 2 grounds alternate on purpose — photo, light, cream, orange, photo, green, light. Two adjacent posts on the same ground blur together in a feed, which is half of why row 1 read flat.

A giant numeral and a headline in the SAME colour merge into each other. Either separate them in space (6b: numeral pushed to x=706, headline ends at 620) or drop the numeral's opacity so it reads as a layer behind. Do not let them touch at equal weight.

Type was the one system never tokenized — colour, spacing, radius and motion all bind to variables, but 478 text nodes carry raw sizes and 43% are off the ramp. A handoff is only as good as its least-tokenized system: the one gap forced the developer onto raw REST JSON for everything.

Type ramp: 26 styles, names identical in Figma and Tailwind (heading/section = text-heading-section). Bind every new text node to a style — 99% coverage is the bar, and the only acceptable misses are nodes with deliberate inline emphasis.
Line heights are still AUTO on all 26 text styles. Set them in Figma first, then add --text-*--line-height pairs to tailwind.css. Do not invent line heights in code.
tailwind.css restates no values. Every @theme entry is var(--token). If a value ever appears literally in that file, the one-way flow has been broken.

Auto-layout IS the fidelity mechanism. Figma's layout properties map 1:1 onto flexbox — layoutMode is flex-direction, itemSpacing is gap, HUG is max-content, FILL is flex:1, FIXED is a hardcoded px. When sizing is deliberate the JSON describes the CSS; when it is a drag artifact the JSON describes a screenshot and the developer has to guess.

Dragging a frame edge silently sets FIXED sizing and looks identical on canvas. Three real bugs came from exactly this: Day-of cards clipping the raffle prices, the nav bar collapsing to 84px, and Event Schedule clipping 'Raffle drawing'. Every one was invisible until measured — run the overflow detector, do not trust the eye.

A clipped child can be caused by a fixed ancestor several levels up. Event Schedule, blocks and every block hugged correctly; the culprit was the 'split' frame two levels above. Walk the whole ancestor chain, not just the node that looks wrong.

Auto-layout DIRECTION cannot be overridden on an instance. Setting layoutMode on an instance child silently no-ops — no error, no effect. Anything that changes direction at mobile needs its own component (hence Footer — Mobile).

Flipping a frame's auto-layout direction INVERTS which axis HUG/FILL apply to. Footer columns were correctly layoutSizingVertical=FILL in a horizontal row; flipping to vertical made that a main-axis fill and collapsed all three to 13px. After any direction flip, reset sizing on both axes explicitly.
Order matters when narrowing to mobile: restructure at full width FIRST, then resize. Narrowing before restructuring squashes columns to ~49px and the layout cannot recover.

Mobile text must be swept to FILL + textAutoResize HEIGHT or it overflows instead of wrapping — desktop text is mostly HUG, which is fine at 1440 and broken at 390. Load fonts first or textAutoResize throws.

Tier Row gained a Device property (Desktop/Mobile) rather than a separate mobile component. This matters: swapComponent to a DIFFERENT component loses every override — text properties AND the per-tier benefit lists. Switching a variant inside the same set preserves all of it. Never solve a mobile layout with swapComponent on content-bearing instances.

Cloning a variant OUT of a component set drops its componentPropertyReferences — the text nodes stop being bound to tierName/price/includes and render the clone's literal text. After adding a variant by cloning, re-bind references explicitly via node.componentPropertyReferences.

Blanket 'release every FIXED main axis' sweeps are destructive — they shrank the 48px hole chips and bullet markers. Only release containers whose content actually overflows, computed from children plus gaps plus padding.

Swapping a component on an instance can leave a dangling node reference that breaks traversal of the whole clone (even reading .children throws). If a frame starts throwing 'node does not exist', delete and rebuild it rather than patching — and stage swaps separately from restructuring.

Mobile needs NO new components for size. Padding on an instance root and text style on an instance child both override cleanly — only auto-layout DIRECTION refuses. Verified: padding 20->12 and text style 28->20 both applied to a live instance.

Mobile type is a parallel ramp ('mobile/' folder), not loose overrides — otherwise mobile loses the tokenization the desktop pages just gained. Display shrinks, body holds at 16: shrinking body hurts the outdoors, in-sunlight reading the brief cares about most.

The component library's own text was never tokenized — only the 478 page nodes were. Component masters carry raw sizes, so rebinding by style id returns 0 there; bind by matching size+family+style instead. Worth tokenizing the library properly at some point.

Argyle Band vectors were constrained STRETCH/CENTER, so ANY width change scaled them horizontally and turned the diamonds into slivers. Now pinned MIN/MIN — a narrower band crops the pattern, which is correct for a repeating motif. Fixing the component re-laid out all 24 instances automatically; no instance repair was needed.

Photos used scaleMode CROP with a hand-authored imageTransform. CROP does NOT re-fit when the frame's aspect changes — it stretches. Any photo that gets reused at a different aspect (desktop 460x470 vs mobile 350x470) must be FILL. Only use CROP when the frame's aspect is fixed forever.
Instance children cannot have x/y overridden (relative-transform is blocked) — but resize IS allowed. Fix positional problems at the component, not the instance.

Footer — Mobile is a CLONE, so desktop footer edits do NOT propagate — content drifts silently. Variants would not fix this either; separate variants are separate components. The real fix is nesting the shared CONTENT as its own component inside both wrappers.

Argyle vectors start at NEGATIVE x (Tall -42/0/-21, Standard -23/0/-11, Trim -12/0) so the pattern bleeds off the LEFT edge as well as the right. Starting at x=0 made the left edge begin on a whole diamond with no dots running off, which read as a mistake. Coverage still exceeds 1440 after the shift.

Figma variant counts are NOT code component counts. Hover/active/focus/disabled are CSS pseudo-states, not props: Button's 30 variants are 1 component with variant x size; Form Field's 24 are 4 components plus an error prop; Tier Row's 7 are 1 component plus a featured boolean. ~15 components total, not 100 variants.

Only FOUR things on this site genuinely need custom CSS: the argyle band, the ticker marquee, the tier-row featured yield, and the nav underline yield. Everything else is Tailwind utilities. Hover lift is NOT one of them.

PROPERTY overrides on an instance permanently shadow the component for that property. Structural changes (adding/removing a child) still propagate, which is why deleting the footer sub-copy carried but changing its padding did not. If a component edit is not reaching instances, check overrides FIRST — the fix is instance.resetOverrides().

Never tune spacing page-by-page on instances. Tune the COMPONENT. Tuning 6 footers individually wrote 15-19 overrides each and silently disconnected all of them from the master. This was self-inflicted and cost a debugging round.

Nav instance overrides are legitimate and must NOT be reset — active state and the Register/Home swap are genuine per-page differences. Footer overrides are never legitimate; the footer is identical on every page.
Standing instruction from Kyle (2026-08-21): delete duplicates and dead components on sight. If it would cause downstream confusion or complicate handoff, rectify immediately rather than asking.

Tier copy lived only as Figma text until 2026-08-21. It now lives in data/tiers.json and drives both the Registration page and the form's tier select. Edit the JSON, not the design, when a price or benefit changes — otherwise the two drift.

Map embed uses the keyless google.com/maps?...&output=embed form — no API key, no billing account. The Maps Embed API (and a key) is only needed for custom styling or markers. Keep the text address above the map: an iframe is not accessible alone and will not render if third-party frames are blocked.
Sponsor ticker is HIDDEN, not deleted, on Home desktop and mobile. It is fully built and tokenized; unhide it as logos arrive through the sponsor form. Do not ship an empty ribbon.
The venue logo under the map IS the outbound link to sanvicenteresort.com — it replaced the 'Get directions' row, so it must be a real anchor, not a decorative image.

Line heights are ratios, not pixels — they scale with the size and survive a size change. The rule: the bigger the type, the tighter it sets. Bullet markers take BODY leading so they align to the text they mark, not to their own size.

Applying line heights makes every text node taller and WILL surface fixed-height containers that were quietly just-fitting. Re-run the overflow detector after — but release only true overflows: the blanket sweep unsquared 36 hole chips and made 42 form inputs auto-width before being corrected. Chips and inputs are fixed controls; they never hug.

body/xs is the HELPER style (form hints, the group-lookup prompt) — 52 uses, all hints. It is the ONE body size that shrinks on mobile: 13 desktop, 12 mobile. The 'body does not shrink' rule protects reading copy; a hint is a label, not prose.

Mobile group cards lay their four player names 2 and 2. A single wrapped line breaks mid-name at 390, which reads as a bug. In code this is a 2-column grid (any name length holds); in Figma the break is authored literally because Figma has no grid-with-separators. Never ship a hardcoded
at a fixed index — pairings change.
HEIC never ships to the web — Chrome and Firefox do not render it. Any phone-sourced photo must be converted to JPG or WebP before handoff.
Carousel filenames ARE the running order. tourney-01..29 encodes it; original camera/Instagram filenames do not. Ship the numbered set or the order is lost.

Assets audit is derived from the FIGMA FILE, not from the folder — count real references. Eyeballing a folder finds what is there; only counting references finds what is MISSING (the glove logo) and what is a decoy (facebook, x, hand-heart).

PNG is for flat colour, screenshots and transparency — never photographs. A photo saved as PNG runs 50-90x the weight of an equivalent JPEG because lossless encoding preserves sensor noise pixel-for-pixel. Converting HEIC is right; converting it to PNG is not.
When converting, go from the ORIGINAL (HEIC) to the target format. HEIC -> PNG -> JPEG compounds loss for no benefit.

The website needs exactly TWO logo files: horizontal negative for the subpage nav, badge for the Home hero. The knockout (neg) is social-only. Do not let a developer pack carry logos the site never references.

Always check file SIZE after a batch conversion, not just that the file exists. Five JPEGs came back at zero bytes — the conversion failed silently on the largest inputs and left valid-looking filenames behind.

Carousel order lives in the FILENAME PREFIX (01-, 02-, …). Slide 01 is 587765888_17906025711272153_8898890657147230087_n.jpg, recorded in the Figma component description, the active-slide layer name, MANIFEST.md and BUILD-SPEC.md.

Mobile-only changes belong on the Device=Mobile VARIANT, not on page instances. Editing the variant reaches every instance; editing instances creates overrides that permanently shadow the component (learned the hard way with the footer).

mobile/body/sm (14/140) is for LIST content on mobile — benefit lines, scannable items. It does not contradict 'body does not shrink': that rule protects prose. A benefit list is closer to a label than a paragraph, same reasoning as helper text.

SUPERSEDES the old 'card is not a link' rule: with the mobile accordion the tier header IS a control (it toggles) and Register Now is a separate action inside the panel. Two targets at different levels, no ambiguity. The original rule existed to stop card hover competing with button hover — that conflict does not arise here.
Accordion height animates with grid-template-rows 0fr -> 1fr, never a hardcoded max-height — benefit lists run 2 to 6 items and any fixed height would clip the long ones.

Document component BEHAVIOUR with labelled instances on the component page, never by duplicating a page frame. A duplicate page is a second copy of all the content and drifts the moment a price or benefit changes — the same failure that hit the footer. Instances cannot drift: they ARE the component.

An all-expanded page would depict a state the product never reaches (a visitor would have to tap all eight). Show the real default — featured open, the rest collapsed — and document the other states on the component sheet.
A control that does nothing must not carry an affordance. SoldOut never expands, so it has no chevron.

HIDE, never DELETE, a node you want absent in a variant. Deleting the benefits node in the collapsed variant destroyed every per-tier benefit list the moment an instance switched to it — seven tiers silently reverted to the component default. visible=false preserves overrides; removal discards them permanently.
The same applies to surplus list rows: a tier with 2 benefits hides the other 4 rather than deleting them, so raising the count later restores rather than rebuilds.

data/tiers.json is not just a dev handoff artifact — it was the ONLY surviving copy of the benefit lists when the Figma overrides were destroyed, and the content was restored from it. Extracting content out of a design file is a backup, not only a contract.

Tier Row has FOUR states: Default, Hover, Featured, SoldOut. Every row looks the SAME at rest — green means the pointer is on it, and nothing else. The featured tier is marked by its ORANGE EDGE alone.

SUPERSEDED: Featured used to be dark green at rest. With eight rows stacked it read as already-selected and stole the meaning of hover. FeaturedMuted was deleted with it — that variant existed only to lighten a dark featured row while another was hovered, and it has no job once featured is never dark. The .tier-list:hover yield rule is gone from components.css too.
Mobile tier rows open INDEPENDENTLY, not exclusively. Opening one does not close another — a visitor comparing two packages should be able to hold both open.

The Figma mobile Registration frame shows tier rows EXPANDED for content review; the product SHIPS them COLLAPSED. These are deliberately different and the canvas carries a NOTE frame saying so. Collapsing the Figma frame to 'match production' destroys the only view where all the tier copy is proofable at once.

The disclosure chevron sits INSIDE the toggle on the header and is present in BOTH states — down closed, up open. An expanded panel with no control reads as un-closable. 'They know they opened it' only holds for the person who just tapped: not for someone who opened four rows and scrolled back, returned later, or arrived on a deep link with a row open.
The chevron must not MOVE between states. It was briefly on the price row when collapsed and absent when open — a control that relocates is a control the user has to find twice.

Chevron is aria-hidden. The button's aria-expanded already conveys state; announcing the icon as well is redundant. The rotated chevron is the SIGHTED equivalent of aria-expanded — dropping it would leave visual users with less state information than screen-reader users.

Mobile tier header carries only IDENTITY + the CONTROL: tier name left, chevron right. The availability badge moved to the PRICE line. Three items on one header line crowded, and with a wrapping tier name the badge and chevron stranded themselves beside a two-line title.

Availability belongs with the money. 'How much / what you get / how many left' is one thought, read at the moment the decision is made. For a sold-out tier the same slot carries the Sold Out badge, which explains the muted treatment instead of leaving it unexplained.
Price and includes are wrapped in a 'money' group so they stay on one line; the badge is pushed right by space-between. Letting 'includes' FILL made it wrap to two lines.

Global navigation must not change shape between pages. Mobile Home used to carry a bespoke hero-nav with inline links while the other five pages used a hamburger — a visitor who learned the hamburger on Tournament Day would not find it on Home. All six mobile pages now use the same nav component.

The mobile bar keeps its horizontal logo on Home even though the hero badge sits directly below. The brief redundancy is the price of an invariant bar, and it matters the moment the bar is sticky: once a visitor scrolls past the hero, the bar is the only branding left.

Home mobile hero is brand + ONE action. Navigation lives in the hamburger; the hero does not repeat it. That is what let the hero drop from 393px to a calmer 383px while gaining breathing room around the badge.

Two photo moments on Home do DIFFERENT jobs and must look different. The hero photo is a GROUND — heavily scrimmed (0.72 to 0.97 green), type sits on it, you do not look at it. The carousel photos are SUBJECTS — bright, unscrimmed, on a green ribbon. Same medium, opposite treatment, so they do not compete.
The hero uses a different image from the carousel's visible slide. Two photo sections showing the same picture reads as a bug.

The full-colour BADGE stays in the mobile hero. It is the primary mark and the one that appears on event signage; the nav bar's horizontal wordmark is the small utility variant. Hierarchy by scale, not by removal.

A hero button feels unanchored when the hero has nothing to say. Adding the date, venue and 'the 2nd annual' above it fixed the float — the button now ends an argument instead of sitting on empty ground.

CROP with an imageTransform is safe when the frame's aspect is FIXED and will never reflow — that is how Grant's portrait zooms to his face at 112x140. It is only unsafe when the same fill is reused at a different aspect.

Mobile prototype links must resolve to 390 frames. Cloning a desktop frame clones its reactions, so every link silently keeps pointing at the 1440 original — check destinations after any clone, the wiring looks correct on the canvas either way.

The Home — 390 hero eyebrow was orange (accent/display) on a photo-over-green scrim. Corrected to text/inverse 2026-08-25. The no-orange-text-on-green rule applies to photo grounds carrying a green scrim too, where the ratio is worse because the ground varies.

A Reaction carries BOTH a deprecated `action` and an authoritative `actions[]` array. Mutating only `action` and calling setReactionsAsync succeeds, reports success, and changes nothing. Write both, then READ BACK and resolve destination names before believing any prototype edit.
Mobile tap targets are 44x44 with the glyph aligned to the edge inside it, not centred — centring the glyph in a larger box moves it and changes a bar Kyle already approved.
Reading `.visible` on some instance children throws "node does not exist" while the SETTER works. Set it and move on; do not gate the write behind a read.

Do NOT build a paint as a placeholder literal plus setBoundVariableForPaint and trust it to render. The matched group card came out pure black that way — bound to color/bg/inverse, rendering #000000. Copy the paint array off a node that is already correct, or set the literal to the token's real value. Screenshot after any paint write.
Desktop tier rows stay EXPANDED (Kyle, 2026-08-25). The accordion is mobile-only. On 1440 there is room for the benefit lists, and the benefit lists are the sell.

Tournament Day Schedule and Format do NOT collapse (Kyle, 2026-08-26). The Groups table earned a collapse because a visitor needs 1 of 36 cards; the schedule is the opposite — every line applies to every visitor, and this is the page someone opens outdoors on the morning of. Collapsing content where 100% is personally relevant just adds a tap.

Tournament Format was tightened instead: four sub-heads, one merged line each, marker hidden (a one-item bullet list is a stray glyph). The second bullet in each block is HIDDEN, not deleted, and its layer name says so.

The confirmation page and the confirmation email are not redundant — the page reassures in the moment, the email is the durable record and the invoice. What WOULD have been redundant is a third touch: a separate invoice document. It was cut.

handoff.blocker: Type is not tokenized: 478 page text nodes, 0 bound to a text style, 204 (43%) at sizes off the 13-style ramp. Off-ramp sizes: 14(89), 22(39), 13(21), 36(16), 18(14), 26(8), 34(6), 24(6), 11(4), 44(1). handoff.stack: Next.js -> React -> Tailwind v4 + shadcn. Token flow is one-directional: Figma variables -> tokens.css -> Tailwind @theme -> shadcn CSS vars via a single adapter file.
handoff.libraryVsCustom: REVISED 2026-08-26 — take as much shadcn as possible. Accordion (Radix) powers BOTH the mobile tier rows and the Groups "View all 18 holes" disclosure, giving aria-expanded/aria-controls/independent state/focus for free. Select, Form+RHF+zod, Button, Badge, Input, Textarea, Label, Carousel all come from the library and get restyled with our tokens. react-dropzone for upload. GENUINELY CUSTOM IS FOUR THINGS: argyle band CSS, the nav underline yield selector, the footer layout, the Groups table. Tier Row is a SKIN over shadcn Accordion, not a from-scratch component.
handoff.shadcnConflicts: shadcn ships shadows (we forbid them), its own neutral palette, its own radius scale, a generic focus ring, and collapses --input into --border when form controls need border/control at 3:1. Override all five on day one; the risk is silent drift on update.
handoff.channel: NO MCP, NO DEV MODE (Kyle, 2026-08-26). Trevor will not run an MCP server and will not buy a Dev seat. LAYOUT-SPEC.md replaces both: every section on every page with padding, gap, direction, width, background token and text style, desktop and mobile. Figma is a picture; the numbers are in the repo. The REST API stays off-limits — it returns coordinates and literal hex with no semantics, which is the original problem.

comms.rosterDecision: Form, delivered through the thread — not either/or. Names typed into an email body have to be hand-keyed into the pairings tab that feeds the Groups page; a form lands them structured. Email replies stay a fallback for stragglers.

The one implied contradiction — invoice email numbering put "Send payment" 01 and "Send your logo" 02, reading as if the logo came after — is fixed: step 02 now says signage goes to print WELL BEFORE the payment deadline.
